The model checks whether the email is registered with known services ‚Äî e.g.,: amazon.in: consistent shopper paytm: active financial tool user flipkart, yatra, jeevansaathi: demographic + lifestyle hints The count and type of platforms help assign a weight to the digital maturity and credibility of the user. Example: User A: Email found on Amazon, Flipkart, Shaadi, and Yatra ‚ûù High digital trust score User B: Email not found on any known platform ‚ûù Flag for manual review or lower trust tier
business_meaning: This attribute acts as a proxy for digital presence, lifestyle stability, and identity legitimacy ‚Äî all of which are powerful, non-bureau indicators of a real and trustworthy user. 1. Identity Authencity - A user with verified accounts on multiple platforms (Amazon, Flipkart, Yatra, etc.) is far more likely to be a genuine, traceable individual. Scammers and synthetic IDs rarely maintain consistent activity across many platforms. 2. Digital Footprint Strength - Broader presence across e-commerce, travel, job, and media platforms shows real-world behavioral signals ‚Äî helping distinguish between a sleeper/throwaway email and a real, active one. 3. Fraud Risk Detection - Low or no presence on popular platforms raises red flags ‚Äî these emails are often used in phishing, promo abuse, or mule operations. 4. Thin-File and NTB / New to Credit users - For users with no bureau history, social platform presence offers alternative validation that they are economically active and reachable. 5. Confidence in Downstream Decisions - Lenders and digital platforms can use the presence score as an input to boost confidence in auto-approval, KYC pre-validation, or contactability scoring.
